issue_context.title: Delaying error reporting by setting classes to be runtime initialized may result in misleading errors
issue_context.body:
**Describe the issue**
Setting classes marked for build time initialization to be initialized at runtime in order to delay error reporting in an effort to catch as many errors as possible may result in reporting misleading `ParsingError`s.

The change happens in https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/ebaa5292081c0c94166dbe0e3aec507ea6c00e4c/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.hosted/src/com/oracle/svm/hosted/classinitialization/ClassInitializationSupport.java#L198

**Steps to reproduce the issue**
```
cd /tmp
git clone --branch 2023-04-05-delayed-error-reporting-causing-issues https://github.com/zakkak/issue-reproducers reproducers
cd reproducers
mvn package
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/jvms/graalvm-ce-java17-22.3.1
$JAVA_HOME/bin/native-image --initialize-at-build-time=. \
  --no-fallback -H:+ReportExceptionStackTraces \
  -jar target/reproducer-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar
```

**Describe GraalVM and your environment:**
 - GraalVM version: **ebaa5292081c0c94166dbe0e3aec507ea6c00e4c**
 - JDK major version: **20**
 - OS: **Fedora 37**
 - Architecture: **AMD64**


**More details**

Which informs us that a method, which we have marked for deletion, is reachable at runtime. However, that's not actually true as we only invoke this method from the static initializer of `Main` which we want to initialize at build time.

To make matters worse, GraalVM not only reports the above misleading error, it also doesn't report the original error that led us here.

review_comments: You can actually remove the field `unsupportedFeatures` and all the code that sets it. And inline away this method.
